answer: Unique-Output Task Registry. Each agent identity must submit a task solution whose output is checked against a global hash store; repeat answers are rejected. To register, an agent mines a copper-seeded nonce binding its identity to an unseen puzzle, so no two identities can share one output. Attackers pay fresh compute per identity plus lost work on collisions. A small nectar reward funds puzzle generation, and any reused relic token from prior rounds is invalidated, forcing new solving cost each time.
